Hi Sam / Priya —

Appreciate the clear list. I put together an initial MAP draft for the technical evaluation milestone and attached it. Key highlights below; the attached is an editable MAP spreadsheet so we can assign owners and dates quickly.

Quick summary (MAP technical milestone - draft):
- Milestone 1 (Week 0): Kickoff & access — Redwood SEs (Ben) and Novacare infra lead to confirm VPN or VPC peering; security questionnaire delivered.
- Milestone 2 (Week 1): Baseline ingestion + sample anonymized dataset upload; Redwood provides a sample harness and test prompts.
- Milestone 3 (Week 2): Benchmark run — latency (P95) target 350ms for 512 tokens, cost target <= $0.003/token (model dependent), quality acceptance via 80% pass on curated prompt set.
- Milestone 4 (Week 3): Results review & decision gate — if benchmarks pass, plan for pilot and target close Q1 2027; if not, recommended follow-ups (quantized model, different routing policy).

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx, redwood-eval-targets.pdf (performance target details).

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to own the benchmark harness and shortlist (see his note below).
2) Novacare to confirm sample dataset access and security contact for SOC/pen test scheduling.
3) Schedule a 30m technical kickoff this week to align on VPN, dataset, and acceptance prompts.

I left placeholders for a target close date of 2027-03-31 but happy to adjust.

Best,
Hannah

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Samuel Jones <samuel.jones@novacare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@novacare.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: technical milestones for MAP

Thanks Hannah — adding the technical specifics for the POC and model shortlist so Novacare can review: 

Technical evaluation plan (short):
- Harness: Redwood will provide a Pytest-style harness + Jupyter notebook for reproducible runs.
- Dataset: up to 10k anonymized notes (small set for throughput/latency + a 200-example curated eval set for quality).
- Models to test (suggested shortlist):
  * redwood-rlhf-2-small (quantized 8-bit) — cost-efficient baseline
  * openlm-7b-instruct (fp16) — good mid-range throughput
  * llama2-13b-8bit (when allowed) — higher quality but higher cost
- Benchmark metrics and acceptance criteria:
  * Latency: P50 / P95 breakdown; target P95 <= 350ms for 512-token context under continuous batching (90% confidence).
  * Cost: per-token inference cost target <= $0.003 for average prompt length (~120 tokens) across the shortlist OR a plan to meet cost through quantization/caching.
  * Quality: 80% pass on the curated prompt set (binary accept/fail per example) OR a demonstrated improvement vs. baseline model by at least 10% on F1-like scoring for key extraction tasks.
- Test infra: We'll run benchmarks from our US region; if Novacare needs EU/APAC parity we can add a regional run.

Dependencies / risks:
- Access to a representative, anonymized dataset (legal/IRB signoff may delay).
- SOC2 evidence and a short security intake (we can front-load the questionnaire).
- If Novacare requires on-prem deployment for the POC, timeline expands by ~2 weeks for networking

I'll own the harness and the runs; Hannah / Marissa — placing the POC milestone owners in the MAP file. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the harness.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-eval-targets.pdf (pdf)]
